outcome: Severe lacerations (third and fourth degree perineal lacerations)
cohort: The study reviewed medical records of 857 women who underwent forceps delivery at term with singleton cephalic presentation from 2010 to 2015.
finding: The incidence of severe lacerations was 10.1%, with birth weight, fetal head station, malrotation, and the number of extractions identified as risk factors, and obstetric anesthesia appearing protective.
mod_finding: The incidence of severe lacerations during forceps delivery was 10.1%, with risk factors including birth weight, fetal head station, malrotation, and number of extractions, while obstetric anesthesia may protect against them.
